newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Kohl to meet Czech premier amid declaration talk.
newsitem.headline: Kohl to meet Czech premier amid declaration talk.

text.p: Czech Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus brushed aside speculation on Thursday about a long-delayed declaration with Germany closing the book on World War Two, but said he would meet Chancellor Helmut Kohl next week.

Kohl said in September he wanted the joint parliamentary declaration, aimed at ending ill-feeling dating from the Nazi occupation and the years that followed, signed by the end of the year but so far no ceremony has been announced.

Klaus refused to say what form any ceremony would take but said he would meet Kohl during a summit of the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) in Lisbon, scheduled for next Monday and Tuesday.

Referring to sessions of the Czech and German parliaments on the declaration, he said: "I do not know whether it will be signed at prime minister level before that. I also cannot say at which moment the parliamentary debates and speeches in the parliaments will start."

But he told a news conference: "My meeting with Helmut Kohl has been arranged during the Lisbon summit. This is the only realistic and concrete information I can provide, everything else is speculation."

Klaus and Kohl rarely meet in each other's capitals, although they hold occasional talks at international meetings, and diplomats have said that their cool personal relationship was one of the reasons for slow progress on the declaration.
Klaus is attending Lisbon in place of President Vaclav Havel, who is due to undergo exploratory surgery for a lung ailment next week.

The declaration aims to address Czech memories of the brutal 1938-45 Nazi occupation and German memories of how the former Czechoslovakia expelled its 2.5 million-strong Sudeten German minority en masse for collaborating with Hitler.
Leaders of the Sudetens and their descendants have repeatedly attacked draft copies of the declaration, and the Czech side has blamed this for delays in its completion.
On Wednesday German government sources said Kohl planned to explain the declaration personally to Sudeten leaders in an attempt to meet the year-end deadline.

The situation has been further complicated by Havel's illness. The Czech president has been a major force behind reconciliation and, unlike Klaus, gets on well with his German counterpart Roman Herzog.
The German government sources said that a signing at government level could be held before the end of the year with parliamentary ceremonies in the New Year.
